originality.rationale: The classical 1996 symmetric-plane perimeter identity p(X)=8/lambda(X) already covers the numerical projection constant as a corollary; no originality is attributed to that value, its maximum, or parameter derivatives. The independently assessed claim is uniqueness among all canonical four-coordinate minimal retractions, with eight active constraints of determinant 64 beta^4. The 1985 regular-polygon article and the recent norm-one stability preprint do not state the unrestricted optimizer-face classification. Related indexed results address a different five-coordinate plane or only symmetry-equivariant minimizers in a different family. Historical uniqueness information in an inaccessible 1976 planar source remains a risk.
residual_risks: Franchetti–Votruba 1976 full text was inaccessible; an older general theorem about uniqueness of minimal projections in polygonal planes, if it exists, might imply the new rigidity statement.
Classical 1996 perimeter identity DOES cover the numerical value and derivatives; these are excluded from novelty.
The uniqueness theorem is for the canonical four-coordinate embedding only, not all possible isometric superspaces.
